Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0002] Guard division with a zero-total check: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator before dividing and return the domain's zero value.
  Compute total_quantity first; if it is falsy (no lines or zero quantity), return ZERO instead of dividing. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' spec and avoids ZeroDivisionError.
- [rb-0003] Read the target file and tests before editing: Before implementing a new function, cat the module, related helpers, models, and any existing tests to match conventions.
  The agent inspected invoice.py, money.py, models.py, and the test file before writing code, which revealed the Decimal-based style and rounding helpers. This upfront reconnaissance led to a first-attempt acceptance.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal math: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers rather than raw arithmetic.
  Inspect money.py first to find conversion and rounding utilities. Wrap raw values with to_money before multiplying, seed sums with ZERO, and apply round_money to the final result so finance rounding policy is honored.

item.title: Match existing error and validation conventions before implementing
item.description: Reading sibling modules to learn the project's error codes and validation patterns produced an accepted implementation on the first try.
item.content: Before writing a new function, grep for existing BillingError raises and isinstance checks in sibling modules. Reuse the same error codes (e.g. invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and message formats so hidden tests and reviewers see consistent behavior.

item.title: Reject bools explicitly when validating integer inputs
item.description: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(quantity, int) alone accepts True/False as quantities.
item.content: Guard integer parameters with `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before range checks. This mirrors the money module's refusal of bool/float and prevents silent acceptance of True as quantity 1.

item.title: Route monetary inputs through the project's to_money helper
item.description: Converting unit_price via to_money before the negativity check inherits the library's float/bool rejection and Decimal normalization.
item.content: When a function accepts a price-like argument, call the existing to_money (or equivalent) converter first, then compare against ZERO. This avoids duplicating type checks and keeps float-poisoning protections consistent across the codebase.
